chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, from Abu Asama, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The perfume is from the Sunnah of the Messengered Prophets.
ai.seo_question: What is the religious significance of using perfume in Islam according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), affirming perfume as a Sunnah of the Messengers, which Shia jurists cite as evidence for its recommended status (Mustahabb) in daily life. This tradition underscores the Islamic emphasis on both physical purity (Taharah) and spiritual refinement, encouraging believers to emulate the Prophetic habit of using pleasant scents to enhance personal dignity and social interaction.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub, from Abu Asama, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The perfume is from the Sunnah of the Mursil Prophetsas’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Yunus ibn Ya’qub from abu Usamah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Using perfume is of the discipline of the Messengers ‘Alayhim al-Salam.’”
